question: 8 years ago, the age of a father was 11 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between Father's age and twice the Son's age 8 years ago = 11.

Each year, this difference decreases by 1 (since father ages by 1, but twice the son's age increases by 2).

In 8 years (to reach present), the difference becomes 11 − 8 = 3.

To make the father exactly twice the son's age, this difference must become 0.

It will take exactly 3 more years for the difference to reduce from 3 to 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**
